'''Clara Torres Latorre''' (born 1997)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://mat.ub.edu/noticies/acte-de-defensa-de-la-tesi-doctoral-de-la-sra-clara-torres-latorre/|title=Act of defense of the doctoral thesis of Ms. Clara Torres Latorre|access-date=14 June 2025|date=21 June 2024|publisher=[[University of Barcelona]]|language=ca}}</ref> is a Spanish [[mathematician]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.laveudalginet.es/actualitat/2018/08/03/desena_medalla_dor_internacional_per_lalgineti_damia_torres_latorre|title=Tenth international gold medal for the Alginet native Damià Torres Latorre|access-date=14 June 2025|language=ca|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180807094700/http://www.laveudalginet.es/actualitat/2018/08/03/desena_medalla_dor_internacional_per_lalgineti_damia_torres_latorre|archive-date=2018-08-07}}</ref> She holds 16 international titles, ten of which are gold medals. This achievement has made her the Valencian student with the best results in history in university-level math competitions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.riberaexpress.es/2014/06/20/damia-torres-guardonat-a-lolimpiada-intenational-mathematical-de-romania/|title=RiberaExpress, Damià Torres awarded at the International Mathematical Olympiad of Romania|access-date=2016-10-03|language=ca|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005070408/http://www.riberaexpress.es/2014/06/20/damia-torres-guardonat-a-lolimpiada-intenational-mathematical-de-romania/|archive-date=2016-10-05}}</ref>

== Career ==
Torres studied the Bachelor's Degree in Mathematics and Physical Engineering at the CFIS of the [[Polytechnic University of Catalonia]] as part of the Estalmat project. In 2014, she achieved gold medals in three high school science olympiads ([[mathematics]], [[physics]], and [[chemistry]]). That same year, she was honored at the [[Palace of the Generalitat Valenciana]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.riberaexpress.es/2014/06/03/lestudiant-dalginet-damia-torres-rep-lhomenatge-de-la-generalitat/|title=RiberaExpress, The student from Alginet, Damià Torres, honored by the Generalitat|access-date=14 June 2025|language=ca|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005081647/http://www.riberaexpress.es/2014/06/03/lestudiant-dalginet-damia-torres-rep-lhomenatge-de-la-generalitat/|archive-date=2016-10-05}}</ref> [[Harold Kroto|Sir Harold Walter Kroto]], [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]], went specifically to the Palace to meet Torres and her teammates.

For two consecutive years, in 2013<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.riberaexpress.es/2014/05/04/damia-torres-guanya-la-xvii-mediterranean-mathematics-competition-a-requena/|title=RiberaExpress, Damià Torres wins the XVII Mediterranean Mathematics Competition in Requena|access-date=14 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005073943/http://www.riberaexpress.es/2014/05/04/damia-torres-guanya-la-xvii-mediterranean-mathematics-competition-a-requena/|archive-date=2016-10-05}}</ref> and 2014, Torres won gold medals in the Mediterranean Mathematics Competition.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.riberaexpress.es/2014/10/28/damia-torres-rep-la-medalla-dor-de-la-mediterranean-matematiques-competition/|title=RiberaExpress, Damià Torres receives gold at the Mediterranean Mathematics Competition|access-date=14 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005074553/http://www.riberaexpress.es/2014/10/28/damia-torres-rep-la-medalla-dor-de-la-mediterranean-matematiques-competition/|archive-date=2016-10-05}}</ref> She also won gold in 2013, in [[Bolivia]], at the Ibero-American Chemistry Olympiad (the greatest achievement in this discipline by any Spanish student).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.colegioquimicos.com/noticia/exitos-estudiantes-valencianos-las-olimpiadas-quimica|title=College of Chemists of Valencia, Successes of Valencian students in Chemistry Olympiads|access-date=14 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005092417/http://www.colegioquimicos.com/noticia/exitos-estudiantes-valencianos-las-olimpiadas-quimica|archive-date=2016-10-05}}</ref> She later added four more golds in mathematics: in 2014, in [[Bucharest]], she earned gold at the International Mathematical Arhimede Contest; in 2015, in [[Puerto Rico]], she won absolute gold at the Ibero-American Mathematical Olympiad,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tusnoticiasdelaribera.com/index.php?option=com_k2&view=item&id=18991:dami%C3%A0-torres-latorre-ha-aconseguit-lor-absolut-a-lolimp%C3%ADada-iberoamericana-de-matem%C3%A0tiques&Itemid=2119|title=Noticias de la Ribera, Damià Torres Latorre wins absolute gold at the Ibero-American Math Olympiad|access-date=14 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005071844/http://www.tusnoticiasdelaribera.com/index.php?option=com_k2&view=item&id=18991:dami%C3%A0-torres-latorre-ha-aconseguit-lor-absolut-a-lolimp%C3%ADada-iberoamericana-de-matem%C3%A0tiques&Itemid=2119|archive-date=2016-10-05}}</ref> leading the Spanish team that finished in third place. That same year, in [[Bulgaria]] at the International Mathematics Competition for University Students, she won another gold. In 2016, she repeated the achievement and also won gold in a speed programming competition in [[Porto]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.tusnoticiasdelaribera.com/index.php?option=com_k2&view=item&id=31765:dami%C3%A0-torres-latorre-ha-conseguido-su-novena-medalla-de-oro-internacional&Itemid=1489|title=Damià Torres Latorre has earned her ninth international gold medal|date=13 August 2017|publisher=Noticias de la Ribera}}</ref>

In 2014, after placing in the top two positions for four years in the Kangaroo Math Contest, Torres Latorre received the Silver Pin, the highest award from the [[Catalan Mathematical Society]] for competitors who earn recognition all four years.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://publicacions.iec.cat/repository/pdf/00000245/00000067.pdf|title=Memory: 2013–2014 academic year|access-date=14 June 2025|date=2017|publisher=Institut d'Estudis Catalans|page=415|contribution=Section: Affiliated Societies}}</ref>
<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ondanaranjacope.com/noticias/id32437-el-campus-de-gandia-acoge-la-entrega-de-premios-de-importantes-pruebas-de-matematicas.html|title=The Gandia Campus hosts awards ceremony for major math competitions|last=Aparisi|first=Inmaculada|date=23 May 2014|publisher=Cope Onda Naranja|access-date=14 June 2025|language=Spanish}}</ref>In 2016, at the 30th Ibero-American Mathematics Olympiad, she also won another gold medal.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://scm.iec.cat/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/N39.pdf|title=SCM. News|access-date=14 June 2025|date=2016|publisher=Scm.iec.cat|page=19}}</ref>

Years later, having fully embraced her [[gender identity]] as Clara, in June 2024 Torres Latorre obtained her PhD in Mathematics on the theory of regularity in obstacle problems of the [[Harnack inequality]], from the [[University of Barcelona]].<ref name=":0"/>
